title: Apply visual changes to auto-hide panel while hidden
line: An auto-hidden panel now shows its current state as soon as it's revealed, instead of first showing the old layout and animating to the new one.
explanation: While an auto-hide panel is hidden KWin stops sending it frame callbacks, so Qt marks the window as not exposed and stops rendering it. Qt Quick only polishes items (which is when layouts like the Task Manager's GridLayout position their children) right before rendering, so changes made while hidden were laid out only once the panel was revealed; the first frame showed the old layout and the tasks' move animations then played in front of the user. PanelView now runs the window's pending polishes from the event loop's aboutToBlock signal while it is visible but not exposed, so layouts and their animations finish while the panel is hidden.

commits.message:
shell/panelview: keep laying out items while the panel is hidden

Items are only polished when a window is rendered, so an auto-hidden
panel showed its old layout when revealed and then animated to the new
one. Now pending polishes are run while the panel is visible but hidden.

BUG: 417783

media.caption: Master: two tasks closed while the panel was hidden; on reveal the panel shows a gap where they were and the last task slides left (slowed 2x).
With the fix, same steps: the panel appears already showing the three remaining tasks (slowed 2x).
Master, frame by frame (33 ms apart) from the first visible frame: the old layout with a gap, then the slide.
With the fix, frame by frame from the first visible frame: the current layout from the start.

reviews.text: Clean, generic root-cause fix in PanelView that flushes pending Qt Quick item polishes from QAbstractEventDispatcher::aboutToBlock while the panel window is visible but not exposed. It avoids re-rendering hidden panels and introduces no polling timers or wakeups, using Qt::QuickPrivate (parallel to the existing GuiPrivate/WaylandClientPrivate dependencies) because Qt offers no public API to polish an unexposed window. The frame-by-frame captures and video convincingly demonstrate that layout updates finish while hidden instead of animating on reveal.
